items.title: Psychology and Time Management in Chess
items.content_text: This article discusses the sense of panic that sets in when the chess clock starts counting down. When time runs critically low, many players stop focusing on the position on the board and instead rush their moves simply to avoid running out of time. It is precisely this loss of composure that often leads to errors they could easily have avoided under normal circumstances.

items.title: Mindset and Aspects Often Overlooked by Chess Players
items.content_text: This article addresses a very common mistake in chess: focusing too heavily on one's own plans while neglecting to observe the opponent's intentions. Through familiar scenarios, the article helps players realize that a good move depends not only on what they wish to achieve but also on how the opponent might respond.

items.title: Stop Looking for the Perfect Move
items.content_text: Every chess player has experienced it. You stare at the board, convinced there's one perfect move that will solve everything. Minutes pass, the clock keeps ticking, and instead of finding brilliance, you end up making a mistake.  The reality is that chess isn't about playing perfect moves—it's about consistently making good decisions. In this blog, we'll look at why chasing perfection can slow your improvement and how changing your mindset can help you play stronger, more confident chess.

Uważał się za mądrzejszego i inteligentniejszego od nauczycieli, dlatego że lepiej od nich grał w szachy. Tymczasem Regina widziała, że jego inteligencja i wiedza ogólna były na poziomie dziesięciolatka. Nie stał się ani odrobinę mniej infantylny, kiedy zaczął dojrzewać, zrobił się tylko jeszcze bardziej arogancki i uparty.
